chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Abu 'Abd Allah al-Kufi, Abu al-Husayn, said: Musa ibn 'Imran related to me from al-Husayn ibn Yazid, from Ibrahim ibn al-Hakam ibn Zuhayr, from 'Abd Allah ibn Jarir al-'Abdi, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) that he used to say:

All praise is for Allah who is neither sensed, nor felt, nor touched. He cannot be perceived by the five senses, nor can imagination grasp Him, nor can tongues describe Him. Everything that is sensed by the senses, or felt by the feelers, or touched by the hands is created. And Allah is the Most High; wherever He is sought, He is found. All praise is for Allah who was before He came into being; 'being' was not found to describe Him. Rather, He was the First Being, whose Creator did not exist. Exalted is His Praise! Rather, the existence of things preceded their existence, so they were as He made them. He knows what has been and what will be. He was when nothing was, and when no speaker spoke of Him, so He was when there was no existence.
ai.seo_question: What are the attributes of Allah regarding perception and existence in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) articulates the Shia doctrine of *Tanzih* (divine transcendence), asserting that Allah is beyond the five senses (*hawas*) and human imagination (*wahm*), distinguishing the Uncreated Creator from all created entities. It highlights the concept of *Qidam* (eternity) and *Baqa'* (perpetuity), noting that God's existence is not contingent upon a maker, thereby refuting anthropomorphism (*Tajsim*) and affirming His absolute uniqueness as the First Being whose knowledge precedes creation.
